text:
The stock fell slightly today despite a strong two-week rally, as oil prices dropped on news that the U.S. suspended new duties on Russian goods, raising expectations that Russian crude will flow back into global markets and ease supply concerns. Brent crude is down sharply from the $110+ spike seen just three days ago when geopolitical tensions in the Middle East were driving prices higher. For a refiner like Marathon, lower oil prices can squeeze profits on the crude they buy and process, even though refineries benefit from the spread between cheap input costs and refined product sales.

The broader shift reflects a pivot away from geopolitical risk premiums—the extra cost added to oil when conflicts threaten supply. With sanctions relief easing worries about tight Russian crude availability, the immediate supply shock fears that fueled last week's rally have faded, taking some of the momentum out of energy stocks.
